translationRepairs: In the fifty-third year the Jiangzhou river dike burst. The emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui and others to go and survey the damage. Cheng was held responsible for failing to dredge the upstream silt buildup, and also implicated because subordinates had extorted Huai salt chest fees; his official insignia were stripped.

In the fifty-third year the Jingzhou river dike burst. The emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui and others to go and survey the damage. Cheng was held responsible for failing to dredge the upstream silt buildup, and also implicated because subordinates had extorted Huai salt chest fees; his official insignia were stripped.
s0010 has 荊州江堤潰; 荊州 is Jingzhou, not Jiangzhou. The prior literal misreads the place-name; the proposed Jingzhou matches the Chinese and the idiomatic field.
In 1795 the Qian Miao chieftain Shi Liudeng rebelled, and the Yongshui Miao chieftain Shi Sanbao joined him. Cheng marched with Governor-General Bi Yuan to suppress the uprising.
In 1795 the Qian Miao chieftain Shi Liudeng rebelled, and the Yongsui Miao chieftain Shi Sanbao joined him. Cheng marched with Governor-General Bi Yuan to suppress the uprising.
s0015 reads 永綏苗石三保; 綏 is sui, so the place is Yongsui, not Yongshui. The proposed romanization corrects a clear error without changing sense.
In the sixtieth year the Qian Miao leader Shi Liudeng rebelled, and the Yongshui Miao leader Shi Sanbao rose in response; Cheng went with Governor-General Bi Yuan to suppress them.
In the sixtieth year the Qian Miao leader Shi Liudeng rebelled, and the Yongsui Miao leader Shi Sanbao rose in response; Cheng went with Governor-General Bi Yuan to suppress them.
The same Chinese 永綏苗 requires Yongsui in the literal field. Yongshui is a romanization error; the proposed replacement is accurate.
He was soon demoted to fourth-rank capital official for an earlier failure in Zhili to uncover false entries in a princely treasury.
He was soon demoted to fourth-rank capital official for an earlier failure in Zhili to uncover false entries in a provincial treasury.
s0045 has 失察籓庫虛收; 籓庫 is a variant of 藩庫, the provincial treasury, not a princely treasury. The proposed provincial treasury restores the correct sense.

Later a Aksu mint clerk stole official money amounting to more than five hundred taels. The official in charge cited the statute on theft by common persons and sentenced him to strangulation after review.

Later an Aksu mint clerk stole official money amounting to more than five hundred taels. The official in charge cited the statute on theft by common persons and sentenced him to strangulation after review.
The literal’s “a Aksu” is ungrammatical before a vowel-initial place-name; “an Aksu” fixes the article without altering meaning. Chinese 阿克蘇 is unchanged in sense.

In Beijing he argued in audience that Yongshui Subprefecture, isolated in the Miao country, could not hold the frontier. He proposed moving the seat to Huayuan, shifting the garrison to Chadong, building blockhouses along the border, turning the old Yongshui town into a garrison post, and posting Miao officers there to control the stockades. The court referred his plan to the responsible offices for action.

In Beijing he argued in audience that Yongsui Subprefecture, isolated in the Miao country, could not hold the frontier. He proposed moving the seat to Huayuan, shifting the garrison to Chadong, building blockhouses along the border, turning the old Yongsui town into a garrison post, and posting Miao officers there to control the stockades. The court referred his plan to the responsible offices for action.
s0100 twice names 永綏廳 / 永綏舊城; 永綏 is Yongsui. Replacing Yongshui with Yongsui corrects the romanization in both occurrences.

On reaching the capital he stated in audience that Yongshui Subprefecture stood isolated in the Miao country and was inadequate for control; he requested moving the subprefectural seat to Huayuan, moving the garrison brigade to Chadong, setting watchtowers and checkpoints all along the border, using the old Yongshui city as a garrison post, and stationing Miao officers in the walled town to restrain the Miao stockades. The matter was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.

On reaching the capital he stated in audience that Yongsui Subprefecture stood isolated in the Miao country and was inadequate for control; he requested moving the subprefectural seat to Huayuan, moving the garrison brigade to Chadong, setting watchtowers and checkpoints all along the border, using the old Yongsui city as a garrison post, and stationing Miao officers in the walled town to restrain the Miao stockades. The matter was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
Literal likewise misromanizes 永綏 as Yongshui; Yongsui matches 永綏廳 and 永綏舊城 and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
